page: The Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a dedicated instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor configured with 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores, running at a base speed of 2.0 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled directly with the instance, providing a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. This server type does not include any GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor demonstrates top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng tests and Geekbench multi-core metrics. The memory architecture delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth for large, potentially uncached blocks, though its Passmark memory score remains in the average tier. The CPU instruction set includes AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and SHA_NI, which facilitate top-tier results in extended instruction tests, physics simulations, and software compilation using Clang.

This server configuration is highly suitable for enterprise database operations, large-scale software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving. It also exhibits strong performance in medium-scale language model inference, specifically for prompt processing and text generation using 7B parameter models. Given the high density of dedicated cores and the substantial bundled NVMe storage, the instance offers excellent qualitative resource density for multi-threaded enterprise workloads without requiring external storage attachments.
